Evidence is conflicting and not sufficiently current or exact: industry commentary cites uncertainty and looming overcapacity, while later company-specific reporting cites a container-freight-rate recovery; the direction and breadth of the cycle are unresolved.

supporting_evidence.claim: Container shipping conditions were described as unstable, with potential excess capacity if Red Sea services resumed.
supporting_evidence.source_title: Container Shipping: Sailing Through Uncertainty And Looming Overcapacity

supporting_evidence.claim: Container freight markets were described as highly volatile, with freight costs changing materially across the cycle.
supporting_evidence.source_title: Are Container Freight Contract Derivatives Finally the Solution to Market Volatility?

counter_evidence.claim: COSCO Shipping Holdings reportedly experienced a sharp quarterly profit rebound as container freight rates recovered, while the sustainability of the upswing remained disputed.
counter_evidence.source_title: COSCO Shipping Holdings stock (CNE1000002J5): earnings rebound and freight cycle in focus

results.primary_cause: Current evidence confirms stronger dry-bulk freight conditions but conflicts on durability and causal quality: rates and Capesize demand strengthened, while BIMCO-linked reporting warns that 2026 strength may be artificial and followed by a supply glut.

supporting_evidence.claim: The Baltic Dry Index reportedly reached 2,732 points on July 31, 2026, up approximately 9.2% during July, with conditions varying by segment.
supporting_evidence.source_title: HTCO Highlights Strengthening Dry Bulk Market as BDI Rises Approximately 9.2% in July and Shipping Equities Gain Investor Attention

supporting_evidence.claim: A key dry-bulk rate measure reached its highest level since December 2023, attributed to rising Capesize demand and tightening vessel supply.
supporting_evidence.source_title: Dry-Bulk Shipping Rates Hit Two-Year High on Capesize Demand

counter_evidence.claim: BIMCO warned that the apparent 2026 dry-bulk strength was substantially artificial due to forced rerouting and could reverse into a 2027 supply glut.
counter_evidence.source_title: Dry bulk shipping faces 2027 supply glut: BIMCO warns Hormuz rerouting boost will reverse
